summary: Intro discovery: AlderPoint evaluating Redwood quickstart with free credits to validate latency and cost tradeoffs before committing to Dedicated or Private. Primary concerns: VPC connectivity, KMS integration, audit logs, data residency; want performance benchmark and SOC2 docs. Agreed to pilot and follow-ups.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Latency vs cost expectations and batching
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Time: 15:00 UTC (46 mins)
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Noah Patel (Redwood), Priya Nair (CTO, AlderPoint), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Marta Ruiz (Security), Benji Park (ML Eng)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): AlderPoint wants to try Redwood API quickstart w/ free credits, evaluate time-to-first-token, and then decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment driven by compliance and latency. SE will share SOC2/KMS notes and Redwood will propose a 2-week perf pilot.

00:00 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate the time, uh quick intros on our side real fast, I'm sophie i'm your AE for redwood inference and with me is diego who's our solutions eng, diego do you wanna say hi
00:18 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): yeah hey all, diego here, i'll be the technical lead for the pilot, we'll cover benchmarks, vpc connectivity, kms, everything, thanks
00:28 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): thanks, priya here, cto at alderpoint, we've been evaluating a couple of providers and wanted to see how fast we can get to first call and what the security posture looks like
00:40 - Speaker 4 (Liam O'Connor): liam, platform team, mostly worried about network, peering, and whether we can keep our data inside our vpc or if we need to route through public endpoints
00:53 - Speaker 5 (Marta Ruiz): marta, security, curious about audit logs, key mgmt, and retention policies, also around soc2 and iso
01:05 - Speaker 6 (Benji Park): benji, ml engineer, will run the inference tests and help define perf targets, nice to meet you
01:15 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): great, goal for today is to understand your constraints, walk quickstart and credits path, and map what a two week perf pilot looks like. feel free to interrupt.

03:02 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): quick put a bookmark on the free credits — the PLG flow gives you a sandbox with X credits we can load, typically that's enough for initial QA and latency profiling. time-to-first-token for the hosted API is usually minutes, assuming keys and rate limits set. if you go private it takes longer to provision, for sure.
03:56 - Speaker 4 (Liam O'Connor): can you be specific about "minutes"? we have a strict demo cutover next week and don't want to waste time, like from signup to a zero-hop api call 
04:12 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): yep, for hosted: create account, get API key, call the endpoints — for a simple prompt you're looking at like 5-10 minutes to first success if you follow quickstart. there can be hiccups with IAM org configs or SSO but it's usually swift.
04:40 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): ok that's promising. primary blockers for us are regulatory — we need either private deployment in our cloud region or strict controls on data egress. what does redwood offer for that?
05:00 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): good question. we have three main modes: hosted api (fastest), dedicated (reserved GPU pools, still managed by redwood but isolated capacity), and private (vpc or on-prem where control plane can be customer-managed). private gives the most control for egress and keys.
05:30 - Speaker 5 (Marta Ruiz): for private, how does kms work? do you support customer-managed keys/HSM? and what about audit logs export to our SIEM?
05:48 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): yes we integrate with customer KMS — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM connectors on request; keys can be customer-managed so redwood never has plaintext. audit logs are exportable to cloud logging or pushed via syslog for our enterprise plans. we'll send the KMS integration doc after the call (note: transcriber often shows as K M S doc or K M S guide).
06:15 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): ok good. latency — we saw some vendors average token latencies of ~50ms but at scale that's different, how do you approach latency vs cost tradeoffs?
06:32 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): couple levers: model choice (smaller quantized models), batching, kv cache/prefix caching, and choosing dedicated instances in a region close to you. dedicated pools reduce multi-tenant noisy neighbor effects. also we can pin model versions so you don't get surprise perf regressions.
07:00 - Speaker 6 (Benji Park): you said kv... did you mean KV cache? (laughs)
07:06 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): yep kv cache — transcribers sometimes write "cash" but yes, caching the prefix/kv state to reduce repeated compute for similar requests, that's huge for cost and latency.

09:10 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): let's talk concrete pilot: we typically run a two-week perf pilot where we give X free credits and a small dedicated pool or hosted baseline depending on the ask. we measure p50/p95 latency, tokens cost, and throughput. then we present a recommendation.
09:35 - Speaker 4 (Liam O'Connor): if we do hosted for pilot, will data leave our region? we're on AWS eu-west-1 and we need EU-only residency for some facets
09:50 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): hosted has region options — we can pin to eu-west-1 in most cases, but for strict data residency and enterprise compliance we recommend dedicated or private deployment. Hosted may store some logs in central telemetry but the customer data path can be region-bound, we'll clarify.
10:20 - Speaker 5 (Marta Ruiz): SOC2 — do you have the report? can we get an MSA with security appendices?
10:33 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): yes we have SOC2 and ISO summaries we can share under an NDA or via our security portal. we'll include SOC2 snapshot in the follow up.

12:02 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): pricing — high-level: what should we expect for the pilot vs production? ballpark numbers?
12:18 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): for the pilot we usually provide credits to cover an evaluation workload — if you want dedicated reserved capacity the pricing shifts to monthly reserved plus usage. hosted is pure usage. i'll send a pricing matrix by tomorrow but ballpark: hosted unit tokens lower start cost but higher variance; dedicated gives better predictability on latency per dollar.
12:46 - Speaker 6 (Benji Park): curious about quantization impacts on accuracy — do you provide recommendations for which models to quantize for cheaper throughput?
12:59 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): yes, optimize module (redwood optimize) gives suggestions. we include sample quality regressions tests, and the se team can run a quick eval on a small prompt set you provide.

15:05 - Speaker 4 (Liam O'Connor): network — can you do VPC peering or do we need to open public endpoints? our security team typically doesn't like internet-facing APIs
15:20 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): for private deployment we do VPC peering and private link like solutions; for hosted we offer private endpoints via our private connector (it depends on plan). we'll need a small set of ips and an aws role/peering info to start.
15:47 - Speaker 5 (Marta Ruiz): also need to know retention policies — logs, payload retention, how long and can we auto-delete?
16:00 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): retention is configurable: for hosted default retention is X days but enterprise/private you can set retention rules and purge. we'll capture your retention policy reqs in the follow up.

18:30 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): sounds like action items are: we share SOC2/KMS docs, pricing, and an outline for the two-week perf pilot. on your side you spin up a test network and send the list of compliance controls. does that look right?
18:50 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): yes, i'll put together the compliance list and timing, priya — i'll try to get it to you by friday
19:12 - Speaker 4 (Liam O'Connor): timeline — if we start pilot mid-april, we need all dependencies by early april to get peering and creds done
19:30 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): sounds reasonable. we'll aim to send docs this week and book a deep-dive on infra next tuesday if that works

22:00 - Speaker 6 (Benji Park): can we get a sample benchmark plan? like what metrics you'll capture and what we should instrument on our side?
22:18 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): yes, sample plan includes p50/p95 latency, tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens, cold vs warm latency (with cache warmed), and a simple correctness/quality pass with your 50 prompts. we'll provide a spreadsheet template.
22:45 - Speaker 5 (Marta Ruiz): auditability question — will we get immutable logs with request ids and token-level traces for debugging?
22:58 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): yes request-level logs with ids, and we can add tracing hooks to tie into your existing APM. token-level traces are stored but access depends on retention and privacy mode — for private you get more granular access.

26:05 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): quick call-out: competitors? we know you eval anthor, coh... anthro? (laugh) any specific reasons?
26:20 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): we looked at Anthropic for safety features and Cohere for embeddings pricing, plus some internal infra options. main reason to talk to redwood is the production serving guarantees and the rollout tooling we liked in the docs.

28:10 - Speaker 4 (Liam O'Connor): legal — procurement will ask for standard msas, do you have templates?
28:22 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): yes we have sample MSA and security appendices, and standard data processing addendum (DPA) for EU. we'll attach those.

30:40 - Speaker 6 (Benji Park): technical nit: how do you handle kv cache eviction and per-customer cache isolation? we want to ensure model state doesn't leak across tenants
30:55 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): isolation is by tenant key and per-pool policies. KV eviction is LRU with TTL and you can pin hot prefixes. in dedicated/private you get stronger guarantees. we'll document the exact behaviour.

33:10 - Speaker 5 (Marta Ruiz): does redwood do vulnerability scans and penetration test reports?
33:24 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): yes we run regular pentests and can share summaries; full reports usually under NDA.

35:00 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): ok i want to recap, and we can nail down dates: 1) redwood sends pricing matrix, SOC2 summary, KMS guide, MSA/DPA 2) alderpoint to provide compliance list and spin up test vpc 3) redwood and alderpoint schedule infra deep-dive and pilot kickoff tentatively week of 2026-04-13 4) run a 2-week perf pilot with a small prompt set and benchmark sheet
35:30 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): that's accurate. one more ask: can we get an estimate for run-rate if we scale to 10k qps on dedicated? even ballpark numbers are fine
35:48 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): that's a big scale and it depends on model selection and batching, we'll include a scaling example in the pricing matrix — for dedicated we give throughput guarantees with reserved shapes.
36:12 - Speaker 4 (Liam O'Connor): any dependencies for the pilot we should be aware of? e.g. IP whitelisting needed, role creation, or legal forms?
36:26 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): IP whitelisting or VPC peering depending on path; for hosted quickstart you just need API key. for private you will need a peering role and some network info.

39:00 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): ok last few minutes, does anyone have other blockers?
39:10 - Speaker 5 (Marta Ruiz): please include data deletion SLA in the docs, we need to show that to compliance
39:20 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): will do, include deletion SLA and retention config options
39:35 - Speaker 6 (Benji Park): can you also include a sample prompt set contract or NDA for test data privacy?
39:50 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): yes we have a testing NDA and we'll attach that as well
40:05 - Speaker 3 (Priya Nair): great, thanks sophie and diego, this was helpful. we should be able to move forward if the docs look good
40:18 - Speaker 1 (Sophie Chen): awesome, next steps we'll email summary + docs and propose calendar slots for infra deep-dive. thanks everyone
40:30 - Speaker 4 (Liam O'Connor): thanks, bye
40:35 - Speaker 2 (Diego Martinez): thanks all, bye

Auto Action items (extracted):
- Send pricing matrix and scale examples (Sophie / Diego)
- SOC2/ISO summary + KMS integration guide (Diego)
- Provide MSA/DPA and NDA for pilot (Sophie)
- AlderPoint to deliver compliance control list and prep network for peering (Priya/Liam)

End of transcript.
